newsitem.title: UK: British Land promoted to FTSE 100 index.
newsitem.headline: British Land promoted to FTSE 100 index.

text.p: Property group British Land Plc will later this month replace retailer Argos Plc in the FTSE 100 index of leading British stocks, the group managing the index said on Wednesday.

In a statement following a quarterly review of the index's members, FTSE International said the market value of British Land at today's close was great enough to propel it into the index, while Argos's value was too small to secure its position.

However others such as building materials group Hanson Plc, sugar group Tate & Lyle Plc and medical supplies firm Smith & Nephew Plc, whose FTSE 100 rank had been at risk, avoided relegation to the second-tier FTSE 250.
Changes to the index will formally take place on March 24.

Composition of UK stock market indexes is re-evaluated four times a year. At the market close on a pre-determined day, firms ranked 90th and above in terms of market value automatically go in while those ranked 111th and below automatically go out.

Membership of the FTSE 100 is traditionally seen as positive for a stock, since it gains a higher international profile and is often bought by "tracker" funds which aim to match the performance of a benchmark index.
FTSE International also announced changes to its other indices. Joining the FTSE Mid 250 are Capita Group Plc, London Forfaiting Co Plc, Chiroscience Group Plc and JJB Sports Plc.
They replace Pace Micro Technology Plc, John Menzies Plc, British Polythene Industries Plc and Henlys Group Plc.
